title: Pairs as a third sleeve
hypothesis: Cointegrated S&P pairs add an uncorrelated third sleeve to the book.
question: With proper atomic legs and equity-based sizing, do cointegration pairs earn enough after costs to join the book?
prior: Pairs trading (Gatev et al. 2006) is market-neutral by construction.
citations: Gatev, E., Goetzmann, W. & Rouwenhorst, K. G. (2006). Pairs Trading. RFS 19(3).
method: Five pre-set variants (v1, v2, + Ornstein-Uhlenbeck half-life gate, + hedge-ratio stability, both).
Gate = net Sharpe > 0.40 and correlation to the book < 0.3.
verdict_reason: Uncorrelated with the book (+0.06), but the best variant earned net Sharpe 0.24 with a −40.8% drawdown. Filtering enough to survive costs left almost nothing to trade.
lessons: A real but small gross edge is still a fail once turnover is paid for.
footer: Research code is private; methods summarised below.
